claims.claim_text: I activated my body-worn camera, identified myself as La Habra Police, and ordered the subject to exit the vehicle.
K9 Officer Murray arrived and deployed the K9 from the vehicle. Murray positioned himself on the east edge of the gate and began issuing K9 warnings through the PA system.
Sergeant Lowe arrived on scene and assumed command. Lowe directed officers to deploy OC rounds.
Prior to deploying OC, the subject revved the engine, turned up the radio, and began yelling obscenities in English from the sunroof.
The subject then placed the vehicle in reverse and accelerated toward the K9 vehicle and officers positioned behind it.
After crashing into the garage bay, the subject drove the Escalade through the metal rollup door and exited onto the street.
Officers Hartman and Ramos moved to the northwest corner of Alpine and Bedford.
The subject raised his right arm toward the passenger-side window.
Officer Murray fired seven rounds from his Colt AR-15A4 rifle. Sergeant Lowe then fired ten rounds from his Glock 21C.
Officer Ramos attempted to fire but her weapon malfunctioned.
I approached the vehicle on foot from the driver's side and observed the subject seated in the driver's seat.
He briefly raised one hand and then closed the window.
Officers then observed the Escalade emerge from the garage at high speed and accelerate eastbound on South Bedford Street.
Officers discovered the business owner, W-1, who had been asleep inside the shop during the entire incident.
At approximately 0301 hours, Sergeant Lowe deployed the first OC round into the vehicle.
